Steps.Description: At Kelpholm's Rider post, Postmaster Dann lays out the commission: 'Tide's three hours off, every third day. Find out why. Pilgrims say omen. I say something big is moving down there.'
Three obvious reads: ask the pilgrims, survey the tide mechanically, or force the issue and draw something up from the deep.
AvailableChoices: talk-pilgrims: Seek out the bogmen pilgrims.
spook-fairgean: Light a fire-signal at the shore. Force a surfacing.

Steps.Description: The off-cycle is mechanically regular: volume displacement suggests a large sub-surface reroute. Something is being built, not thrashed.
Time to close. Three routes remain.
AvailableChoices: commune-fairgean: Signal for a Fairgean parley — respectfully.
leave-and-report: Report what you have. Do not close.

Steps.Description: Thirty feet down, a Tide-Eater — a Fairgean maintenance-beast — is rerouting a deep current as nest construction. It notices you.
AvailableChoices: kill-beast: Kill it. Fast and loud.
spare-and-redirect: Redirect the current. Spare the beast.

Steps.Description: The Tide-Eater dies loud. Tide is restored. A current you never saw goes slack, and something far down makes a noise that is not a song.
